questions.q: Spatial data has two components. What are they?
questions.why: The location says where a feature is, using a coordinate system. The attributes are the non-spatial variables about what is there.

questions.q: Why are Census Bureau or USGS data called "authoritative"?
options: They are always more accurate than any other source
Formal institutions rely on them as trusted, decision-relevant data collected by experts with standardized methods
questions.why: Authoritative refers to who collects the data and how, and to the fact that governments rely on it. It doesn't mean the data is error-free.

questions.q: Which of these is crowdsourced spatial data?
questions.why: Crowdsourced data is collected on purpose by non-experts. OpenStreetMap, Mapillary, eBird and iNaturalist are the reading's examples.

questions.q: Restaurant locations with a star rating attached to each point are an example of...
questions.why: The rating is a mark: extra information attached to each location.

questions.q: Why is Census data released as areal data, such as tracts and block groups?
options: Points are too hard to map
Aggregating protects the privacy of individuals
Areas are more accurate than points
questions.why: The Census always aggregates its data to some areal unit so that it doesn't reveal information about individual people.

questions.q: Which data model represents space as a grid of equal-sized cells?
questions.why: Raster data is a grid of regularly spaced pixels. It fits continuous phenomena like elevation or temperature, which the field view describes.

questions.q: Of the three vector primitives (point, line, polygon), which is the only one with an area?
questions.why: A polygon closes on itself: three or more points where the first and last coordinate pair are the same.

options: a set of files, such as .shp, .shx, .dbf and .prj
an open standard from the Open Geospatial Consortium
questions.why: The geometry, index, attribute table and projection live in separate files that must travel together. GeoPackage is the open, single-file alternative.

questions.q: A raster with 1 m pixels compared to one with 30 m pixels has...
options: the same resolution, because resolution depends on the sensor
no resolution, because only vectors have resolution
questions.why: In raster data, resolution is the pixel size on the ground. Smaller pixels capture more detail, which means higher resolution.

options: everything is related to everything else, but near things are more related than distant things
spatial data always follow a normal distribution
questions.why: This is why spatial data break the classical assumption that observations are independent.

questions.q: Wolf territories spaced to avoid neighbors are an example of...
questions.why: Territorial species keep their distance to reduce competition, so the pattern is more evenly spaced than random. That is negative autocorrelation.

questions.q: A spatial process is non-stationary when...
options: the way it operates changes from place to place
questions.why: If a relationship differs across space, a single global model can miss it. Geographically weighted regression estimates the relationship locally instead.

questions.q: Poverty rates have a standard deviation of 13.82 across NC zip codes but 6.58 across counties. This illustrates...
options: the zone effect of the MAUP
the scale effect of the MAUP
questions.why: Larger units average away local variation. When results change with the size of the units, that is the scale effect.

questions.q: Which is the best way to reduce MAUP problems?
options: Always use the largest units available
Match the areal units to the scale of the process you think is at work, and check results with similar units
questions.why: Patterns depend on scale, so pick units that fit the hypothesized process and test whether results hold at, say, block group and tract levels.
